content:
More than a year after cameras were rolling inside Fort la Reine Museum, viewers will finally get to see what happened when an Indigenous-led paranormal investigation team spent the night exploring the historic site in Portage la Prairie.

Season 5 of Ghost Hunters of the Grand River premieres today, September 2, on APTN and YouTube, featuring the investigation by SNIPE (Six Nations Investigating Paranormal Encounters).

And while viewers may be expecting to see unexplained voices, shadowy figures or other strange activity, there’s one group who will be watching with just as much curiosity as anyone else: the museum staff.

Fort la Reine welcomed SNIPE to the museum when the episode was filmed, but they weren’t there for the overnight investigation, meaning they have no idea what the cameras captured.

“They left their cameras on overnight to record. We have no idea what happened or what they found, so we can’t wait to watch it,” community outreach coordinator and fundraising manager Cindy McDonald says.

That makes today’s premiere a bit of a reveal for the people who know the historic museum village best.

Related stories:

  • Indigenous ghost hunters film at Fort la Reine
  • A night of history, mystery and a few unexplained moments at Fort la Reine Museum
  • ▶️ Listen to this news story on the radio: Country 93 / Mix 96 / CFRY 920

Back to where the investigation began

Fort la Reine has developed a reputation among paranormal enthusiasts, with visitors and investigators reporting everything from unexplained voices to shadowy figures and other unusual experiences throughout its historic buildings.

The museum has previously hosted the Winnipeg Paranormal Group, and its connection with that group helped bring SNIPE to Portage la Prairie for an episode of Ghost Hunters of the Grand River.

When SNIPE arrived last year, the Indigenous-led team spent the night investigating the museum, using cameras, audio recorders and other equipment to search for signs of paranormal activity.

The visit was part of filming for the show's fifth season, and the team left cameras running overnight to capture anything that might happen after they had left the buildings.

Now, viewers will finally get to see the results.

A different way to see the museum

For Fort la Reine staff, the episode is another opportunity to showcase the historic site from a perspective visitors don't normally experience.

The museum's historic buildings are typically explored during the day, when visitors can learn about the people, businesses and communities that helped shape life on the Prairies.

An overnight paranormal investigation offers something quite different.

Rather than knowing exactly what the cameras may have captured, museum staff plan to watch the episode together during a small viewing party.

It will be their first chance to see the investigation unfold, and discover whether SNIPE found anything unusual inside their museum.
